0.0.n: Combines with ぶら to describe strolling around town in the title.

0.1.n: Short for ぶらぶら, suggesting wandering casually; here it is not a form of ぶる.

0.2.n: An English loanword used as part of the title 街ぶらトーク.

0.3.n: 証 refers to proof or identification, here a card showing membership.

1.0.n: The prefix お adds a friendly, polite touch to 友達.

1.1.n: An English loanword introducing the friend's assigned identification number.

1.2.n: This is an identification number, so the leading zeros matter.

2.0.n: Explicitly addresses the person receiving the membership card.

2.1.n: Marks あなた as the person the following statement is about.

2.2.n: Identifies Nagai's occupation before his name.

2.4.n: This is the family name in 永井佑一郎.

2.5.n: This character begins the given name 佑一郎; it is not a separate word here.

2.6.n: These characters complete the given name 佑一郎; they are not a separate name here.

2.7.n: Marks Nagai as the person you became friends with; the sentence continues on the next line.

3.0.n: Japanese does not mark singular or plural here; お makes 友達 sound friendlier or more polite.

3.1.n: Marks the resulting relationship before なる, meaning to become.

3.2.n: The polite past form of なる describes a completed change in relationship.

4.0.n: Sets the time frame for the request that follows.

4.1.m: linking part of 今後とも
4.1.n: Here と belongs to the fixed expression 今後とも, not the usual use meaning with someone.

4.2.n: In 今後とも, も adds the sense of continuing the relationship into the future.

4.3.n: With お願いします, this forms a conventional request for goodwill rather than a literal instruction.

4.4.n: A polite request expression that completes the friendly formula よろしくお願いします.

5.0.n: A polite acknowledgment of what was just said.

5.2.n: The polite past form of 分かる commonly acknowledges that you understand an explanation or instruction.

6.1.n: This is the family name in 永井佑一郎.

6.2.n: This character begins the given name 佑一郎; it is not a separate word here.

6.3.n: These characters complete the given name 佑一郎; they are not a separate name here.

6.4.n: Marks the person the speaker became friends with.

6.5.n: The prefix お adds warmth or politeness to 友達.

6.6.n: Marks the new relationship reached through なる, meaning to become.

6.7.n: The polite past form of なる appears inside the sentence the listener is asked to repeat.

6.9.n: A conversational quotation marker identifying the exact words to say.

6.10.n: The て-form of 言う plus ください makes a polite request.

7.0.n: This is the family name in 永井佑一郎.

7.1.n: This character begins the given name 佑一郎; it is not a separate word here.

7.2.n: These characters complete the given name 佑一郎; they are not a separate name here.

7.3.n: Attached to the name, 君 signals familiarity and is often used for boys or men.

7.4.n: Marks Nagai as the person the speaker became friends with.

7.5.n: The prefix お gives 友達 a friendly, polite tone.

7.6.n: Marks the resulting relationship in お友達になる.

7.7.n: The polite past form of なる announces the newly established friendship.

8.0.n: The core expression of gratitude; the following ございます makes it more polite.

8.1.n: ござい is the connecting form of ござる used before ます in this fixed expression.

8.2.n: Attaches to ござい to complete ございます and make the thanks polite.

0.tip: 街ぶらトーク is the title; 会員証 identifies the item as its membership card.

1.tip: お友達 adds a warm, friendly tone to what is essentially a membership number.

2.lit: As for you, with comedian Nagai Yuichiro...
2.tip: The final と means with, linking Nagai to the friendship described in the next line.

3.tip: お友達になる means to become friends; に marks the resulting relationship.

4.lit: From now on too, favorably I ask you!
4.tip: 今後ともよろしくお願いします is a set phrase asking for continued goodwill, here continued friendship.

5.tip: 分かりました is a natural polite way to acknowledge understanding an instruction.

6.lit: Please say, I became friends with Nagai Yuichiro.
6.tip: って marks the quoted words, and 言ってください asks the listener to say them.

7.lit: I became friends with Nagai Yuichiro, familiar suffix!
7.tip: 君 after the name adds familiarity; it is not the word for you here.

8.tip: Treat ありがとうございます as one polite expression of thanks despite the subtitle's word divisions.
